learningObjectives: Generate Instance combinations automatically at both the Attribute level and the TestSheet level.
Identify the documented generation targets and distinguish generated datasets from instantiated and executed tests.
Explain why a StraightThrough must be marked before generating with Linear Expansion.
Distinguish Generate Instances from Complete Instances when a TestSheet changes after combinations already exist.

elements.description: Generate Instances produces design datasets from Attributes and their values. These rows are not executed tests; template mapping and instantiation are separate steps. Choose the method and scope according to required coverage, rather than assuming automatic generation establishes completeness.

Right-click a TestSheet, TestCase-Design Class or Attribute and choose Generate Instances with the desired method. You can Ctrl-select specific Attributes or Instances for a narrower scope. The documented default maximum is 1000 combinations; generation is not promised to be instantaneous for every dataset.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generating at an Attribute or selected scope

elements.description: The generation article documents TestSheet, Class and Attribute targets without requiring a manually created empty folder. The Instances article states that creating the first Instance in an Attribute automatically creates its Instances Collection. The historical add-then-delete folder workaround is not established as a universal prerequisite by these accessed articles.

For a selected scope, hold Ctrl while selecting the Attributes or Instances, right-click one of them and choose Generate Instances followed by the method. Inspect the generated combinations and unused values; do not assume all other Attributes were included.

elements.text: Linear Expansion requires a defined StraightThrough path. It builds baseline variations by switching one StraightThrough choice for a non-StraightThrough choice. Define and inspect that baseline before generating; the accessed docs do not describe a guaranteed fallback or exact error dialog when it is absent.

bulletPoints: Generate at a documented TestSheet, Class or Attribute target; Ctrl-selection can restrict the scope.
Define the StraightThrough path before choosing Linear Expansion.

elements.description: Right-click the TestSheet and select Generate Instances followed by the desired method. Inspect the resulting combinations, nested data usage and scope. Generated rows are held in an Instances Collection beneath the relevant TestSheet.

elements.text: Keep relevance and verification distinct: BusinessRelevant = Yes marks business-relevant data (the default), No marks non-business-relevant data, and Result is used for verification. Sub-Attributes inherit a changed parent relevance. Result is not an instruction to skip assertions. The accessed articles do not fully specify a universal exclusion algorithm for every generation method.

bulletPoints: Inspect the generated rows and Instance Usage; generation alone is not test execution.
Use Result data to express verification; fill and bind the expected values appropriately.

elements.description: Use Generate Instances for generation with the selected method. When additional values need to join existing combinations without duplicates, the documented operation is Complete Instances. The accessed article does not justify calling every Generate operation a destructive rebuild.

Complete Instances combines values not previously combined, without creating duplicates. Uncombined Instances appear in bold. Right-click a TestSheet, Class or Attribute, select Complete Instances, then choose the method. Inspect the resulting coverage; this does not guarantee completeness beyond the chosen method and scope.

bulletPoints: Complete Instances adds previously uncombined values without duplicates.
Inspect the method, selected scope and resulting usage; do not equate rows with passed tests.

elements.text: Independent exercise: generate a small unconstrained dataset, add a new value, then use Complete Instances and inspect usage and duplicates. Compare selected-scope generation with whole-sheet generation. Original Academy videos/exercises require access and have not been verified.

examPitfalls.title: Treating an unverified folder workaround as a universal prerequisite
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming every Attribute generation requires manually creating and deleting a first Instance.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use documented generation targets and inspect the installed version. The accessed article does not establish this manual empty-folder requirement; the first manually created Instance automatically creates its collection.

examPitfalls.title: Generating with Linear Expansion before marking a StraightThrough
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Running Generate Instances with Linear Expansion selected, without any Instance flagged as StraightThrough.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define a StraightThrough path before Linear Expansion. Do not assume Tosca chooses a random baseline or falls back to All Combinations.

examPitfalls.title: Using Generate Instances after adding a new Attribute to an existing TestSheet
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ignoring the documented duplicate-avoiding completion operation after adding new values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Complete Instances combines previously uncombined values without duplicates; inspect resulting coverage rather than assuming every Generate call destroys or rebuilds the existing data.

examPitfalls.title: Treating Result data as irrelevant to assertions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Leaving expected outcomes empty because verification data is not the business input being varied.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Result denotes verification data. Define and bind expected outcomes separately from the business-input variations; generation is not a successful test result.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which objects are documented targets for Generate Instances in Tosca TestCase-Design?

options.text: Only Class references with no Attributes.

practiceQuiz.hint: The generation operation applies to design data containers.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The generation article names TestSheets, TestCase-Design Classes and Attributes as targets. Template instantiation and execution are separate operations.

optionExplanations.A: Templates bind design data to executable tests; they are not the sole design-generation target.
optionExplanations.B: These are the three targets explicitly listed for Instance generation.
optionExplanations.C: The documentation does not restrict generation to empty Class references.
optionExplanations.D: ExecutionLists organize execution; this operation targets TestCase-Design objects.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester plans to generate combinations with Linear Expansion. What must be defined first?

options.text: Tosca automatically picks one Instance per Attribute as StraightThrough.
A StraightThrough path to use as the baseline.
It behaves exactly like All Combinations instead.
Nothing — StraightThrough is irrelevant to automatic generation.

practiceQuiz.hint: Linear Expansion substitutes non-baseline choices one at a time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documentation requires a StraightThrough path before Linear Expansion. It does not promise automatic baseline selection or a fallback to another method.

optionExplanations.A: The documented prerequisite is a defined path, not an automatic arbitrary selection.
optionExplanations.B: The method expands from this baseline by replacing one choice at a time.
optionExplanations.C: All Combinations is a different selected method, not a documented fallback.
optionExplanations.D: The baseline is fundamental to Linear Expansion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Additional values have not yet been combined in a TestSheet that already contains combinations. Which documented operation adds these without creating duplicates?
practiceQuiz.hint: Look for the operation specifically documented for uncombined values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Complete Instances combines previously uncombined values without duplicates. Choose the method and inspect scope and resulting coverage; it does not establish executed or passed tests.

optionExplanations.A: Generate is the general generation command; Complete is the operation specifically documented for this duplicate-avoiding update.
optionExplanations.B: Complete Instances addresses previously uncombined values without creating duplicates.
optionExplanations.C: Arrange Instances organizes existing data rather than completing missing combinations.
optionExplanations.D: Resolving a Class reference changes sharing, not combination coverage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which BusinessRelevant setting identifies an Attribute and its sub-Attributes as verification data?

options.text: An Attribute with more than three Instances.

practiceQuiz.hint: Expected outcomes have a distinct relevance role from business inputs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Result marks data used for verification. Yes marks business-relevant data, and No marks non-business-relevant data. A verification role does not remove the need for assertions.

optionExplanations.A: Yes marks business-relevant data; the distinct verification role is Result.
optionExplanations.B: Result is the documented verification setting for the Attribute and its children.
optionExplanations.C: Instance count does not identify the verification role.
optionExplanations.D: No denotes non-business relevance, not the verification setting.

quickRecap.value: Focus on a level, right-click → Generate Instances, choose the combinatorial method.
TestSheet, Class or Attribute targets are documented; no universal manual empty-folder workaround is certified here.
Generate the selected method, then inspect rows and usage; datasets are not executed tests.
StraightThrough Instances must be marked BEFORE generating.
BusinessRelevant = Result denotes verification data, whose expected values still need assertions.
Combines previously uncombined values without duplicates; inspect the selected method and scope.
